A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MSU-Bench and contain the same 150-score inventory and 1,800-question benchmark. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original zero-shot evaluations, LoRA adaptation experiments, level-wise success rates, question-presentation comparisons, and MMLU evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains original model evaluations and additionally reports title-only diagnostic results and statistical comparisons between human and LLM judgments.

M1.justification: The benchmark formulation, ABC/PDF representations, LoRA adaptation strategies, visual-encoder freezing rules, and three-model majority-vote judging remain unchanged. V2's additional prompts and inference descriptions document procedures without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The musical-score inventory, four question levels, and MMLU coverage remain unchanged. V2 adds a title-only scenario without score input in Table 3, testing answerability from title cues. WildScore is discussed as related work, rather than evaluated as an additional dataset.

E2.justification: V2 removes Qwen2.5-VL-3B-, 7B-, and 32B-Instruct from the reported full-benchmark visual comparison. It also omits the 3B and 32B models from the question-by-question versus batch comparison. The remaining comparator sets are retained; the additional textual baselines in v2 Table 5 were already in v1 Table 2.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a title-only control and human-versus-LLM grading validation. The stated 90/30/30 split, LoRA training budget, and single-run full-benchmark evaluation remain unchanged. Newly supplied decoding settings are disclosures; v2 does not clearly establish whether the question-presentation protocol changed for its revised fine-tuning results.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends benchmark-validity analysis with a title-only diagnostic testing superficial guessing and a human comparison testing the reliability of automated grading. Existing modality, LSR, and MMLU analyses remain. The question-presentation analysis is condensed, retaining overall results for eight models while dropping two models and the level-specific breakdowns.

E5.justification: V2 adds Pearson correlation and McNemar significance testing for human–LLM evaluation agreement. Existing Wilson 95% confidence intervals and single-run reporting remain unchanged. No increased run count or new seed study is reported, and the agreement analysis does not specify its sample size.

E6.justification: V1 Table 3 is replaced by v2 Figure 5 with materially different fine-tuning values: Qwen3-4B's adapted Level 1 accuracy changes from 66.67% to approximately 31%, and ABC replaces PDF as the strongest adapted input modality. These are changed reported results, not established same-setting performance declines. V2 adds title-only scores and judge agreement results (r = 0.805, p < 0.001; McNemar p > 0.05), while removing visual baseline rows and level-specific prompting results. Retained zero-shot scores, MMLU results, LSR plots, and prompting overalls match.

T1.justification: The LSR definition and Wilson confidence-interval expression are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and the newly reported statistical tests introduce no new formal derivation.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution (5) reverses direction: v1 claims separate questions perform better and hierarchical scaffolding is not effectively used; v2 claims joint questions perform better and models can effectively use hierarchical reasoning. The benchmark novelty, modality-gap, adaptation, and general-knowledge-retention claims otherwise remain.

C2.justification: V2 reverses the interpretation of question batching, adds model-scaling and visual-noise explanations, and interprets its new diagnostics as evidence of score dependence and grading reliability. It also introduces an educational application rationale and explicitly limits coverage to Western art music. Long-score exclusions are retained limitations already disclosed in v1 Appendix E.

D1.justification: New Appendices K–M and O document inference frameworks, decoding parameters, deterministic judging, exact prompts, annotation conventions, and recruitment of ten volunteer doctoral annotators. The abstract announces public release without providing an access location. Conversely, v1's first-movement and 300-bar curation rules and explicit question-by-question fine-tuning evaluation description are no longer stated; this does not establish that those procedures changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds WildScore to related work and the benchmark-feature comparison, together with citations supporting the new diagnostics, statistical tests, and implementation tools. The existing related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning are largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, research-question descriptions, case study, and results narrative undergo substantial rewriting and compression. V2 reorganizes supporting material into descriptively titled appendices, expands several appendix discussions, and adds dedicated Limitations and Acknowledgements sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, adds a curation/evaluation diagram and title-only table, replaces the fine-tuning table with six bar-chart panels, and converts two prompting tables into one overall-accuracy chart. It also splits the baseline table and relocates MMLU and visual LSR displays. Several retained figures are resized or moved without changing their data.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful grading validation, a title-only control, exact prompts, and explicit scope limitations, and better aligns the batching discussion with retained results. However, v1's precise fine-tuning table becomes a chart with substantially different values and no equally explicit question-presentation specification, while detailed prompting results disappear. These changes improve documentation in some areas but reduce the auditability of central experiments. The PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
